mustHaveNodes.name: list
mustHaveNodes.comment: list() is emitted with label Method (class member). Confirmed empirically: fn.decorators = ['Get:list'] (parseDecoratorStrings' 'Name:arg' encoding — decorator name 'Get', arg 'list'). The 'decoratorContains' field is a dedicated matcher check (list-membership, not exact prop equality) since fn.decorators is a string list, not a scalar the generic props subset-match can compare directly.

mustHaveNodes.label: APIRoute
mustHaveNodes.comment: APIRoute nodes have no 'name' property (matched by nodeKey/props only); matcher must allow name to be empty/absent when props alone identify the node. nodeKey = models.APIRouteNodeKey('GET','/items/list') = 'api:GET:/items/list', confirmed empirically.

mustHaveEdges.comment: run(ops: PdfOps) calls ops.generate('doc'); the only concrete implementation in this fixture is PdfGenerator, and the call graph resolves directly to PdfGenerator.generate. Verified empirically via plain scip-typescript indexing (no resolver needed).

Type-level IMPLEMENTS, produced natively by scip-typescript (detectionSource=scip) — NOT the CODEGRAPH_TS_RESOLVER structural resolver. PdfGenerator's `implements PdfOps` clause causes scip-typescript to emit an is_implementation_of relationship directly; verified empirically the resolver script was skipped in this run ('resolve.mjs not found') and the edge was still present with detectionSource=scip, confirming the plain SCIP path is sufficient here.

Method-level IMPLEMENTS: PdfGenerator.generate -> PdfOps.generate, detectionSource=scip (native scip-typescript path, matches tiny-ts golden.json's ConsoleLogger.log -> Logger.log shape exactly). nodeKeyContains disambiguates the two same-named 'generate' Method nodes (concrete PdfGenerator#generate vs interface member PdfOps#generate).

Construct 4: formatName is a const-bound arrow (export const formatName = (n) => n.trim()), promoted from Variable to Function by promoteDeclaratorBoundFunctions (kind_promotion.go) because its SCIP definition occurrence sits inside a declarator-widened function node of the same name. greetUser calls it directly. Verified empirically: formatName appears as a Function node (not Variable) with inDegree=1.

Construct 5: main.ts imports doWork from './facade' (a bare re-export `export { doWork } from './impl'` with no local binding), and callDoWork() calls it. Verified empirically via direct Cypher on the Reference/Symbol graph BEFORE the call-graph builder ran: the Reference node at main.ts covering the call site links directly to the ORIGINAL src/impl.ts doWork() SCIP symbol, not to any facade.ts phantom symbol — scip-typescript itself resolves re-exports transparently at the reference level. The resulting CALLS edge lands on impl.ts's doWork, confirming no phantom re-export node is created. NOTE: the original fixture design called doWork() at TOP-LEVEL module scope in main.ts; that produced ZERO CALLS edges for ANY top-level call in the file (also true for run(), Paginator(), etc.) because the call-graph builder only attributes CALLS edges to an enclosing Function/Method — top-level statements have no enclosing node. The fixture was corrected to wrap the call in an exported function (callDoWork) so this construct actually exercises re-export resolution instead of silently testing nothing. This top-level-attribution behavior is itself arguably a gap (see report) but is out of scope for this construct's assertion.

Construct 3: decorator-routed handler. @Controller('items') + @Get('list') on ItemsController.list must produce APIRoute{method:GET,path:/items/list,detectionSource:decorator} plus this EXPOSES_API edge. Verified empirically via direct Cypher after indexing without any nestjs/common package installed — only ambient .d.ts declarations for Controller/Get (see src/decorators.d.ts) were needed for scip-typescript to index the file; the decorators are never invoked at runtime so no real framework implementation is required, only that they parse and resolve as decorator syntax.

Module-scope call attribution: `export const registration = registerThing()` runs at import time, so the FILE is the caller. This is the exact gap construct-5's comment documented ('top-level statements have no enclosing node ... produced ZERO CALLS edges'), now asserted as fixed.

mustNotHaveEdges.comment: THE 767-NOISE REGRESSION CLASS. Options has only optional members (page?, onDone?: () => void) — per tsresolver.go's SkippedNoRequiredCallable rule, an interface with no REQUIRED function-typed member is universally/near-universally assignable and must be skipped by the structural resolver entirely, never producing an IMPLEMENTS edge. Paginator structurally matches Options' shape (same two optional members) but does NOT `implements Options` in source. Verified empirically in TWO configurations: (1) plain scip-typescript path (resolver not invoked, resolve.mjs not found in this environment) — 0 IMPLEMENTS edges touch Options at all, confirmed via direct Cypher; scip-typescript itself never emits is_implementation_of for structural-only matches, only for explicit `implements` clauses, so Options is safe on the native path regardless of the resolver. (2) See labeled_test.go's CODEGRAPH_TS_RESOLVER-guarded subtest for the resolver-path re-verification — if the resolver runs, this same assertion is re-checked against its output; if the resolver cannot run in this environment, that subtest SKIPs with a clear message rather than silently passing. 'from' is omitted (matches ANY source node).
Symmetric check: Paginator must not be the source of ANY IMPLEMENTS edge (it implements nothing in source — no `implements` clause at all).
Module-scope VALUE reference (`export const savedRef = valueOnly`) must not fabricate a CALLS edge from any node.
In-body VALUE reference (`const h = bodyValue` inside useBodyValue) must not fabricate a CALLS edge from any node.
